title: 2024 operating budget review and strategic investment options
subtitle: Library and Centre in the Square budgets, user fees, enterprise dividends, and the new Strong Mayor budget timeline.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a special meeting on the draft 2024 operating budget. The minutes record no motions, so the committee made no recommendations. Members gave feedback to the Mayor, who will table the budget on December 4, 2023 under the Strong Mayor legislation.

Staff proposed a 3.9% property tax rate increase, below inflation of about 4%. With utility rate increases, this is a combined annual increase of $124 for the average household. The Kitchener Public Library and Centre in the Square presented base operating grants within the City's 3.9% guideline.

Staff described $1M of unallocated funding against 10 strategic options totalling $2M. Several members supported Cameron Heights Pool access, trail connections, technology improvements and playground replacements. Some raised concerns about more cycling funding. Staff set 2024 enterprise dividends: Golf eliminated, Parking reduced from $2M to $1.4M, and Gas held flat.

Councillors must send proposed amendments to the Clerk by December 11, with a final budget meeting on December 14. A Special Finance and Corporate Services meeting on November 27 will cover the capital budget and public input.
debate: Several councillors favoured directing active transportation money to trails, such as curb cuts, crossings and wayfinding signs, rather than more cycling lanes. Staff said the proposed cycling funding finishes the downtown grid and works alongside federal housing funding.
Some councillors asked for more traffic calming, saying it is the most common complaint from residents. Staff said the budget reflects earlier increases and the level of need they identified.

Members agreed that $2M of options cannot fit within $1M. One councillor suggested looking at reserves, other funding sources or the base budget. Another urged members to stay within $1M, and staff said unfunded options would return later.

On the Library's pilot of collections in community centres, a councillor asked to add Kingsdale Community Centre and suggested a one-year pilot. Staff said a two-year pilot would give better data, and offered an update to Council after one year.

On enterprises, staff said Golf has run a deficit for about a decade and Parking has lost demand since remote work grew. Councillors asked how long Parking would take to recover. Staff expected two to three more difficult years.

Councillors wanted a clearer way to show residents how the City's share of the tax bill compares with the Region and school boards, since regional increases are larger. Staff said they could prepare this.
